AUDIT.md.title: Draco — code audit

headings.text: A-1 ·                           throws in the packaged bundle *[verified]*
A-2 · Four settings are read from disk, shown in the UI, and never reach the engine
B-1 · Partial downloads are written to one directory and cleaned up from another
B-2 · Every completed download is copied rather than renamed when temp and destination are on different volumes
B-3 · Plain YouTube tasks cannot refresh an expired media URL
B-4 · A periodic queue re-fires its completion action forever
B-5 ·                    loses the destination and half the task's metadata
B-6 · Two forced journal flushes can race over a shared        path
B-7 · Cat mode (once A-2 is fixed) has several problems of its own
B-8 · The Go host's log rotation was written as a constant and never implemented *[verified]*
B-9 ·              children can rename themselves out from under the mux
C-2 ·              is created inside the install directory *[verified]*
C-3 · Packaging config is duplicated and inconsistent
C-4 ·                      is a build output with no clean guarantee
D-1 · Session cookies for every download are persisted in plaintext, indefinitely
D-2 · The ffmpeg fallback source is unverified
D-3 · A failed antivirus scan is advisory only
D-4 · No SSRF guard on takeover URLs
E-1 · "Download all links" spawns one host process per link
E-2 ·                  serializes every queue twice, every 30 seconds

links.context: - Written: [`task.ts:156`](src/main/engine/task.ts:156) — `this.config.tempDir || this.task.dir`, and `tempDir` is always supplied (`manager.ts:361`, `:413`).

Note the asymmetry that hides this: `createHlsRunner` at [`index.ts:231`](src/main/index.ts:231) does **not** pass `tempDir`, so HLS parts land in `task.dir` and *are* cleaned up correctly. Only the plain-file path is broken.

`.dracoTemp` lives on the install volume; downloads usually go to the user's chosen drive. `moveFile` ([`naming.ts`](src/main/engine/naming.ts)) correctly falls back to copy-and-delete on `EXDEV`, so a 40 GB download is read and rewritten in full after it finishes — minutes of disk time, and it needs 2× the space transiently.
[`manager.ts:557–661`](src/main/engine/manager.ts:557). Currently unreachable, so these are latent:
- **`uniquePath` is TOCTOU.** ([`naming.ts`](src/main/engine/naming.ts)) Two tasks finishing at the same instant can both be handed the same free path; the second `moveFile` overwrites the first.
- **`pumpUntilDone` has an unreachable `break`** ([`task.ts`](src/main/engine/task.ts)): the preceding `if (!segmenter.complete) throw` makes it dead.
- **The `ServerBusyError` docblock sits above `HttpStatusError`** ([`worker.ts:33–41`](src/main/engine/worker.ts:33)) — the comment describes the class below it, not the one it is attached to.

- **`icons.ts`' docblock claims the CSP is `img-src 'self' data:`**, but [`index.html`](src/renderer/index.html) actually sends `img-src 'self' data: https:`. Either tighten the CSP (nothing needs remote images — every icon arrives as a data URL) or fix the comment.

- **Chrome's `storage.onChanged` handler drops the dedupe/cap** that `prefsReady` applies to `excludedChannelIds`/`excludedVideoIds` ([`extension/background.js`](extension/background.js)), so the in-memory copy can exceed the bounds the initial load enforces.

[`hls/ffmpeg.ts`](src/main/hls/ffmpeg.ts) — the gyan.dev source carries `sha256Url` and is checked. The BtbN GitHub fallback has none, so a ~170 MB binary is downloaded and executed on TLS trust alone. GitHub publishes checksums for those releases; wire them up, or drop the fallback.

[`manager.ts`](src/main/engine/manager.ts) — when `scanFile` rejects (which is how a scanner reports a detection), the file is already renamed to its final name and the task is already `done`. All that happens is `task.detail` gets a sentence. Nothing quarantines, deletes, or marks the task as failed. If this is intentional the comment should say so; if not, a non-zero scanner exit should at minimum move the file aside and set `status: 'error'`.

`validateUrl` ([`create.ts`](src/main/engine/create.ts)) accepts any `http(s)` URL, including `127.0.0.1`, RFC1918 addresses and `.local`. A page can invoke the extension's link-click path with such a URL and have Draco fetch it with browser-supplied cookies. Low severity for a download manager — the response only lands in a file — but the extension is explicitly an untrusted input path, and a private-address denylist is a few lines.

Documented honestly in [`preallocate.ts`](src/main/engine/preallocate.ts), so this is a note rather than a finding: on an elevated run, unwritten regions of a `.dracodl` contain whatever the previous tenant of those clusters left. If a download is abandoned partway, that data sits readable in the part file. Worth a line in the user-facing docs.

`sendUrls` in [`extension/background.js`](extension/background.js) loops `await callHost(...)` per URL, and `chrome.runtime.sendNativeMessage` starts a **fresh `draco-host.exe`** for each call. Two hundred links is two hundred sequential process launches, two hundred pipe connections, and two hundred appends to the unrotated `host.log` (B-8).

[`scheduler.ts:160,171`](src/main/queue/scheduler.ts:160) — `JSON.stringify(this.queues)` before and after, purely to detect change. Cheap today; it scales with `taskIds`, which grows with the download list.

[`extension/background.js`](extension/background.js) — that event fires several times per navigation, and each call reaches `stateForTab` → `pageIdentity` → `chrome.scripting.executeScript` in the MAIN world (for YouTube URLs). `refreshAllTabs` does it for every open tab at once. Debounce per tab.
